articles.title: Australia trimmed mean CPI rises to 3.7%, above forecasts, as RBA hike case firms
articles.desc: Oil is the clearest driver of the headline beat, and Bullock tied higher energy prices directly to a worse inflation outlook only minutes before the release, so any further rise in crude adds to the case for tightening. The bigger signal for markets is the core reading. A trimmed mean that rose to 3
articles.content: Oil is the clearest driver of the headline beat, and Bullock tied higher energy prices directly to a worse inflation outlook only minutes before the release, so any further rise in crude adds to the case for tightening. The bigger signal for markets is the core reading. A trimmed mean that rose to 3.7%, when the RBA had expected it to stabilise, supports pricing for a hike on November 2 and 3, and backs the Australian dollar and front-end yields. The slightly softer weighted median takes a little off that, but not enough to change the overall message. AUD/NZD traders also face the RBNZ decision at 01:00 GMT, where a widely expected hike could limit any relative move in the Aussie. --- Earlier: RBA’s Bullock: oil shock means inflation above August forecasts, Board meets next week --- Australia’s core inflation picked up instead of levelling off, landing just as Governor Bullock was telling senators that inflation is running above the RBA’s forecasts. Summary: Q3 trimmed mean CPI rose 1.0% q/q (expected 1.0%, prior 0.8%) and 3.7% y/y (expected 3.6%, prior 3.6%). Q3 headline CPI rose 1.3% q/q, above the 1.2% forecast and up from 0.6%. September CPI rose 0.8% m/m (expected 0.7%) and 4.3% y/y (expected 4.2%, prior 4.0%). The monthly trimmed mean rose 0.3% m/m and held at 3.6% y/y, both in line with forecasts. The Q3 weighted median rose 1.0% q/q, slightly below the 1.1% forecast, and 3.6% y/y. The data came as Bullock said inflation will likely exceed the RBA’s August forecasts. The Board meets on November 2 and 3. Australia’s underlying inflation rose more than expected in the September quarter, with the Reserve Bank of Australia’s preferred trimmed mean measure climbing to 3.7% year on year, strengthening the case for another rate hike when the RBA Board meets on November 2 and 3. The trimmed mean, which strips out the largest price rises and falls to show the core trend, rose 1.0% in the quarter, in line with forecasts and up from 0.8% in the June quarter. The annual rate of 3.7% was above both the 3.6% expected and the June quarter’s 3.6%. The quarterly pace also ran ahead of the roughly 0.8% implied by the RBA’s August forecasts. Headline CPI rose 1.3% in the quarter, above the 1.2% forecast and more than double the 0.6% rise in the June quarter. The monthly figures pointed in the same direction. Headline CPI rose 0.8% in September, above the 0.7% forecast, lifting annual inflation to 4.3% from 4.0% and above expectations of 4.2%. The monthly trimmed mean rose 0.3%, in line with forecasts, holding at 3.6% year on year. The weighted median, another underlying measure, was a little softer, rising 1.0% in the quarter against a forecast of 1.1%. The data landed while RBA Governor Michele Bullock was appearing before a Senate committee. In her opening statement, delivered shortly before the release, she said inflation was likely to run higher than the RBA’s August base case, as the re-escalating Middle East conflict has pushed energy prices well above earlier assumptions and the labour market appears a little tighter than previously judged. She said a key question for next week’s meeting is whether the tightening delivered so far, 100 basis points this year, will be enough to bring inflation back to target in a reasonable time. Today’s figures add weight to that concern. The RBA still uses the quarterly trimmed mean as its main gauge of underlying inflation, and a rise in the annual rate, rather than the stabilisation the central bank had forecast, suggests price pressures are broadening beyond fuel. Higher energy costs are lifting headline inflation directly, while the firmer core reading points to the domestic capacity pressures Bullock highlighted. The RBA will publish updated forecasts alongside its decision next week, which will show how far it has revised its inflation outlook and whether it sees the need for further tightening. --- I think the comments from the RBA we've head (see link above as well as Hauser and Hunter last weekalong with today's data locks in a rate hike next Tuesday: This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.content: Bond named a Leader in Loyalty Services, Q4 2026 Evaluation by Independent Research Firm Privately held loyalty and customer engagement company recognized for its strategy, capabilities, customer feedback, including ability to connect global strategy with local execution – , the global, customer intelligence-driven engagement company, has been named a in The Forrester Wave™: Loyalty Services, Q4 2026. Bond believes this recognition underscores its sustained performance and fifteen years of participation in the independent research firm's evaluations. According to the report, "Bond's solid vision is rooted in building growth and intelligence ecosystems for their clients to help them shift from 'small L' program loyalty to 'big L' brand loyalty." Forrester also notes that Bond is "a strong fit for enterprises seeking a loyalty and CRM partner that blends intelligence, behavioral science, strategy, and execution across complex ecosystems," and that customers praise Bond's "ability to connect global strategy with local execution." "We believe this recognition reflects one simple truth: the customer relationship is the center of how brands grow. Customers don't see a difference between a loyalty program, and a brand's emails, app, employee interaction, or service, and neither should the brands that serve them," said Morana Bakula, President & CEO, Bond. "Connected loyalty is bigger than points; it means growing lifetime value, keeping the best customers longer, and using what known customers reveal to find more customers like them. That is the work Forrester evaluated: loyalty, CRM, and customer intelligence operating as one growth engine, and, for us, it's a perfect reflection of the value we aim to create for our clients." The Forrester Wave™ is Forrester's evaluation of the top vendors in the market, based on a rigorous, transparent methodology that includes detailed questionnaires, executive briefings, case studies, and interviews with reference customers. The Loyalty Services, Q4 2026 evaluation assessed seven providers across their current offering and strategy. Among them, only two were named a Leader. Bond continues to set the pace in the loyalty industry, broadening the definition to one that better reflects what customers value. "Loyalty at Bond has always been more than a points program; it's a business growth strategy that connects customer intelligence, emotional engagement, and value creation. Being named a Leader in Loyalty Services adds to an already eventful year for Bond, and, we believe, speaks to our leadership, capabilities, and impact in the industry," added Morana Bakula. Bond recently acquired , a UK-based, award-winning CRM marketing agency, deepening its CRM craft and further expanding its European footprint to support global brands in building connected loyalty. "Programmatic loyalty is under pressure from every angle: members are active in only half of the programs that they join, and that number hasn't moved in a decade," added Sean Claessen, Chief Strategy Officer, Bond. "The next S-curve isn't more points. It's connectivity and intelligence… it's a wider value exchange that makes loyalty relevant across more of a customer's life and feeds into everything from acquisition to retail media. That's the vision Forrester evaluated, and it's the work we're doing with clients every single day." Previously, Bond was recognized as a Strong Performer in The Forrester Wave™: Loyalty Platforms, Q4 2025 for its loyalty platform technology, making Bond one of the few companies that Forrester has assessed on both the technology and services sides of loyalty. Whether powering programs on its own platform or connecting the technologies that brands already own, Bond's approach is the same: loyalty strategy and the systems that deliver it, working as one. articles.title: Embarrassment isn't why scam targets stay silent, Heimdal survey finds
articles.desc: A survey of 1,884 UK scam targets found 7.2% who didn’t report blamed embarrassment. A former Dorset Police cybercrime detective says every report helps.
articles.content: Embarrassment isn't why scam targets stay silent, Heimdal survey finds There were 2,510 press releases posted in the last 24 hours and 501,937 in the last 365 days. Embarrassment isn't why scam targets stay silent, Heimdal survey finds Shame gets the blame, but it isn't the real reason most scams go unreported. A survey of 1,884 UK scam targets found 7.2% who didn’t report blamed embarrassment. A former Dorset Police cybercrime detective says every report helps. LONDON, UNITED KINGDOM, October 27, 2026 / / -- Embarrassment sits near the bottom of the reasons people give for not reporting a scam, according to a survey of 1,884 UK adults targeted by a scam in the past 12 months. Of those surveyed, 42.7% didn’t tell their bank, the police, or the website or app where the scam happened. The most common reason, given by 47.2%, was that they hadn’t lost anything, so it didn’t seem to matter. Just 7.2% said they were embarrassed, fifth of the six reasons named. More than a quarter (27.8%) didn’t think reporting would make a difference, and one in five (20.5%) didn’t know who to report it to. People could give more than one reason. Almost a quarter (24.4%) told only family or friends, and 17.4% told no one at all. Women were more likely than men to keep it to family or friends, at 28.8% against 19.7%. The picture was different for people who lost money. Of those, 11.7% didn’t tell their bank, the police, or the platform, against 49.9% of people who lost nothing. “What I want to call out, as probably the most important piece of this report, is that four in 10 people don’t report a scam,” said Adam Pilton, cybersecurity advisor at Heimdal Security and former cybercrime Detective Sergeant with Dorset Police. “During my time in the police, investigating cybercrime, I found time and time again that intelligence was the lifeblood of my investigations. When it comes to cybercrime investigations, you often have very little information to go off. “That is why the reports from other people were impactful. Maybe the same telephone number or email address had been used across multiple separate scams. All of this feeds into the investigations and enables law enforcement to identify and bring to justice those involved in these crimes.” The National Cyber Security Centre says that as of September 2026 it had received more than 59.6 million scam reports, and about 264,000 scams had been taken down across 466,300 web addresses. Adults aged 25 to 34 lost money most often. Among 25 to 34s targeted by a scam, 35.7% lost money, more than five times the rate for over-65s (6.8%). Calls pretending to be a bank, the police, or the government reached 60.5% of 18 to 24s who were targeted, against 36.0% of over-65s. People in full-time work also lost money more often than everyone else (23.7% against 11.9%), a gap that held once age was taken into account. “This report caught me by surprise, particularly when I looked at who lost the money,” said Pilton. “The highest percentage of individuals that lost money were those aged between 25 to 34. But maybe more surprisingly, the lowest were those over 65 years in age. Only 6.8% of that category had lost money to a scam. “I find this surprising due to the cases that I’ve dealt with and where the proportion of money is in our society.” In London, 27.0% of people targeted by a scam lost money, against 16.8% across the rest of the UK. - In England, Wales, and Northern Ireland, report fraud to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or on 0300 123 2040 - In Scotland, call Police Scotland on 101 - If you’ve lost money, contact your bank straight away, or call 159 - If you get an unexpected call about your money, hang up and call 159 to reach your bank - Forward scam emails to report@phishing.gov.uk https://heimdalsecurity.com/blog/uk-scam-report-gap Heimdal commissioned the survey and Pollfish ran it. articles.title: PM Modi's vision giving fresh momentum to India's science, innovation ecosystem: Experts
articles.desc: New Delhi, Oct 27 (IANS) Experts, scientists and startup founders attending ESTIC 2026 on Tuesday praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's emphasis on science and technology, describing his address at the event as inspiring and aligned with India's aspirations of becoming a developed and self-reliant
articles.content: New Delhi, Oct 27 (IANS) Experts, scientists and startup founders attending ESTIC 2026 on Tuesday praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's emphasis on science and technology, describing his address at the event as inspiring and aligned with India's aspirations of becoming a developed and self-reliant nation. Christopher Parmar, CEO and Co-Founder of space-tech startup Orbitt Space, said the event provided an opportunity for innovators and entrepreneurs to directly engage with the Prime Minister and showcase their work. He noted that his company had the chance to brief Modi about its activities and vision. Singhan Ganguly, an independent researcher, AI specialist, data scientist and software engineer, described the Prime Minister's speech as highly motivational and said his contributions towards promoting research and innovation have encouraged greater participation in scientific fields. Custom Ad: Multiplex Dr. Karthik Subramanian from the Rajiv Gandhi Centre for Biotechnology (RGCB), Thiruvananthapuram, said the government's support for science and technology has been encouraging for the research community and has created a positive environment for scientific advancement. Echoing similar views, Dr. Vikram Singh of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) said India is emerging as an important global player and expectations from the country are rising both domestically and internationally. "There are many senior scientists present here whom you can also speak to. However, considering the needs of the country, India is emerging on the global stage, and people both within India and in other countries have high expectations from our nation. To fulfil these expectations, all scientists are striving to follow the path and vision laid out by our Prime Minister and take forward his efforts," he noted. Shovik Mukherjee, a scientist at the National Institute of Biomedical Genomics (NIBMG), said PM Modi's inaugural address highlighted India's progress towards the goals of 'Viksit Bharat' and 'Atmanirbhar Bharat'. Gaurav Shriram Patil, a PhD research scholar at the H.R. Patel Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research, described participation in the conclave as a valuable opportunity and credited the leadership of Prime Minister Modi and Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh for promoting platforms that bring together researchers from across the country. --IANS pk

articles.title: Science is successful only when it benefits society: PM Modi
articles.desc: PM Modi urges translating science to societal impact, backing ₹1 lakh crore R&D funding to accelerate innovation from lab to market.
articles.content: Science is successful only when it benefits society: PM Modi - The Hindu Subscribed with another email? Logout and Login with that one. Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription Science is successful only when it benefits society: PM Modi Prime Minister urges researchers to take innovations from laboratory to land and ensure measurable outcomes - October 28, 2026 07:09 am IST - NEW DELHI Prime Minister Narendra Modi visits a startup exhibition stall and interacts with an innovator at the inauguration of Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026 at Bharat Mandapam on October 27, 2026 | Photo Credit: ANI on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) said science succeeds only when it travels from the laboratory to the land and improves people’s lives. Addressing the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC), he said it must not become “merely a forum for discussion” but should deliver measurable outcomes. Mann ki Baat address: PM Modi promotes ‘Vocal for Local’, highlights India’s scientific progress Mr. Modi said India’s science and technology story has long been one of catching up with other countries, but in the 21st century the country has emerged as a leader in scientific and technological developments. He said, “The discovery of zero showed that India has a culture of discovery. Chandrayaan’s landing near the lunar south pole, Mangalyaan’s success on the first attempt, and the vaccines developed during the COVID-19 pandemic are examples of this.” The audience at the conclave comprised three Nobel Laureates, top technocrats of India’s scientific establishment, startup founders and scientists from both India and abroad. Mr. Modi said a country’s technological capabilities depend on its research. He said efforts are underway to “speed up” the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF). Referring to research funding, he cited a commitment of ₹1 lakh crore, including ₹12,000 crore for taking research from the laboratory to the market, with private investors partnering equally. He also referred to new commitments of ₹24,000 crore. The number of patents filed in India had risen from about 50,000 to 1.5 lakh, Mr. Modi said, describing this as evidence of a strengthening culture of innovation rather than merely an increase in number. India backing high risk, high impact R&D projects: PM Modi On Artificial Intelligence (AI), he posed what he called an “important question” about how to exercise scientific judgement in the age of AI. “Science works by questioning paradigms and looking at problems with fresh eyes,” he said. “AI can perform routine tasks quickly and raise productivity, but should not limit scientists’ thinking or independent thought, and its answers must meet the accuracy standards of scientists.” Referring to the birth anniversary of nuclear scientist Homi J. Bhabha on October 30, Mr. Modi said a developed India will need large quantities of nuclear energy. He noted that the 500 MW Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) has reached first criticality, strengthening the country’s long-term energy position. India an emerging global powerhouse, needs world-class leaders across all sectors for accelerated growth: PM Modi He also pointed to Indian space start-ups, a rocket made in India that placed a satellite in orbit on its first attempt, and the country’s satellite docking capability. Indian-made AI chips are reaching other countries, an AI model has been built domestically, and work is underway on battery technology based on Indian raw materials, he said. The needs of sectors ranging from nuclear energy to space to AI and semiconductors differ, he said, but India’s emerging technologies are rising together. Describing India as a young country with vision and imagination, he said it needs a generation capable of leading in technology. He summed up the guiding principle as: “We will do it.” Sign-up/manage your newsletter subs

articles.title: This lava planet shouldn’t have an atmosphere—but it does
articles.desc: TOI-561 b may be a supercharged version of Venus or Jupiter’s moon, Io. The post This lava planet shouldn’t have an atmosphere—but it does appeared first on Popular Science.
articles.content: This lava planet shouldn’t have an atmosphere—but it does | Popular Science TOI-561 b is fascinating to observe from 280 light-years away—but it’s not a place anyone would want to visit. Not only is it blanketed by an , but TOI-561 b is constantly bombarded by destructive radiation from its host star. The planet endures so much stellar energy that astronomers have long assumed its atmosphere evaporated eons ago. (JWST) contradict those initial conceptions. After examining TOI-561 b for 37 hours—almost four complete orbits—researchers now believe the planetary lava lamp actually features a thick atmospheric shell. The surprising evidence recently detailed in isn’t what scientists assumed from a planet under such stellar duress. “Our discovery challenges current theories,” . “We would expect a heavily irradiated rocky planet like TOI-561 b to have lost its atmosphere billions of years ago.” Like Earth’s moon, TOI-561 b is tidally locked, which means its rotation coincides almost exactly with the time it takes to orbit its star. This ensures one side of the planet constantly experiences daylight, while its other half is always enveloped in darkness. JWST’s extensive observation window allowed Piette and her colleagues to study TOI-561 b’s phase curve—how its brightness and heat shift during its orbit. However, the results didn’t make sense. The planet’s dayside was cooler than it should be, while the nightside didn’t account for the temperature difference. “[We] revealed that the planet reflects a significant amount of light from its star, and that heat is being redistributed around the planet instead of only on the sunlit side,” explained University of Waterloo astrophysicist and study co-author . “Together, these point to the presence of an atmosphere.” It’s likely not a thin layer of clouds, either. “The evidence suggests it still has a significant atmosphere today,” added Piette. Computer simulations of TOI-561 b’s climate indicate that its atmosphere is possibly composed of silicate minerals like silicon dioxide and magnesium silicate. If true, these would hypothetically reflect much of the harmful stellar radiation away from the planet’s surface. Regardless, the discovery creates more questions than it answers. It could be that TOI-561 b simply began with a huge quantity of gas. Another theory contends that the planet-wide molten ocean functions like a single, gigantic volcano that continually supplies gas into its atmosphere. Armed with the new data, astronomers next hope to determine whether TOI-561 b resembles a hotter version of that reflects about three-quarters of starlight, or if it operates like a superpowered iteration of Jupiter’s . Either way, JWST will be called into service once again. “Observing the planet at longer wavelengths with JWST could give us insights and help explain how a planet this hot has held on to an atmosphere for billions of years,” said Dang. 2026 Popular Science Home of the Future Awards 39 products that will improve your everyday life.
